title: yaml parser on ill-formed YAML
notes: Fixed (spec docs/error-reporting/specs/E-PARSER.md). The two memory addresses are gone with the `repr(exc)` that produced them, and with them the nondeterminism that only the harness normalizer was hiding -- Hygiene 1 to 3. Switching to `str(exc)` was rejected as the whole answer: PyYAML renders `in "<unicode string>", line 1, column 6`, naming a file that does not exist. So `parser_yaml_diagnostic` reads `exc.problem`, `exc.problem_mark` and `exc.context_mark` directly, exactly as `yaml_diagnostic` already does for `.pdl` files, and renders the position in the `output:N` gutter, which says whose line 1 it is. PyYAML's own snippet renderer is never used. `_recognize` is shared with the file-level YAML diagnostics rather than duplicated; it gained one parameter, `line_phrase`, which rewrites the `line N` in its `help:` texts into `line N of the block's output`. The default is the identity, so no existing golden moves, and the parameter takes the rendered phrase rather than the number so that the one range case (`lines 1-3`) goes through it too. Fix stays at 1, which is the honest score for this reproducer: `_recognize` has no branch for `expected ',' or ']'`, so it falls to the generic arm -- PyYAML's problem string as the caret label, `check the syntax at line 1 of the block's output` as the action. The `'<stream end>'` token in the label is the one wart left on the page. A `_recognize` branch for unclosed flow collections would fix this entry and file-level E-PARSE-001 together and is listed as adjacent work in the spec, not folded in here. The rule paragraph concatenates the parser's own rule with `_recognize`'s when it has one, so a tab inside a block's output reads `... a single YAML document. YAML allows only spaces between tokens.`
